title: 0.6.1 RETEST: does fasting tolerance move consumer viability at identical config?

identity.note: The probe always ran from the current checkout. A historical arm spec applied here is a settings replay, not a reproduction of its original figure.

preregistration.hypothesis: Engine-contrast test, not a config test: identical settings to graze-viability (which scored cons 11/18, prod 13/18 on 0.6.0), executed on 0.6.1 where starvation damage ramps over 6 deficit ticks. If consumer failure was variance-intolerance, replacement should rise with per-capita intake flat (conversion, not subsidy).
preregistration.prediction: cons > 0 on at least 12/18 AND prod > 0 on at least 12/18 seeds at tick 6000 (both machine criteria — consumer bar requires +1 over 0.6.0's 11/18; producer bar 12/18 admits one seed of slippage from 13/18). Human-read: consumer B/D distribution shifted up vs the 0.6.0 viability run with per-capita graze intake (grazeEnergy/pop) flat. Coexistence rate NOT predicted.
preregistration.falsification: FALSIFIED if cons > 0 on fewer than 12/18 (no improvement over 0.6.0's 11/18): fasting tolerance does not convert to viability. If consumers improve while per-capita intake rises, the mechanism is subsidy-like, not conversion — report as confounded, not supported.
preregistration.notPredicted: Coexistence rates, capture shares, extinction counts (descriptive), decomposer endpoints.
confoundsControlled: Settings byte-identical to graze-viability (same lifts, same 15 slots incl. rsur 30, same 18 seeds, same horizon); the ONLY difference is the engine (0.6.0 -> 0.6.1)
Matched engine contrast: any rate/B-D/intake difference is attributable to fasting tolerance
conservation enforced per seed at 0.5%; a seed above it fails the run rather than reporting

criteria.statement: consumers > 0 at tick 6000 on at least 12/18 seeds
producers > 0 at tick 6000 on at least 12/18 seeds
